# Code Map — Dispatcher (Admin Web App / Dispatch Console)

Next.js 16 / React 19, mostly API-backed with mock remnants. components/Console.tsx is a
two-level shell: the Home.tsx launcher, then one apps/*App at a time, each rendering NavRail
with its own group (manifest in lib/apps.ts; lib/nav.ts derives NAV_GROUPS from it). Styling
is inline style objects driven by lib/theme.ts tokens — no Tailwind/CSS modules.

- BookingPolicy.tsx is a 30-line page frame around screens/settings/BookingPolicyPanel.tsx, moved out of Settings.tsx (now five tabs — Budget Codes left too, it lives in the Budgeting console).
- Reports.tsx is a ~60-line shell switching between screens/reports/ClientAccruals.tsx and TerminusSummary.tsx; the report tab bar and the pseudo-table cellStyle/headerRowStyle both live in screens/reports/shared.tsx.
- screens/booking/BookingDetail.tsx has NO ScreenId — it is selection state inside Bookings.tsx (same pattern as Fleet/Clients), retained across a trip Home as `communityBooking.bookingSelId` in CommunityBookingApp; pass print/email gating comes from lib/booking/passes.ts passIssuance (Confirmed only, payment never gates), the booking-lifecycle button rules are local to the file.
<!-- notes:dispatcher-screens:end -->

<!-- notes:dispatcher-components:start -->
- Console.tsx is a two-level shell: Home.tsx (the launcher tile grid, gated per role by lib/apps.ts) → one apps/*App.tsx at a time, each rendering NavRail with its own group and screens; only tripSelId stays hoisted in Console, everything else is per-app via lib/appState.ts. apps/shell.ts is the Shell/AppProps contract every app takes; NavRail's `groups`/`onHome` and TopBar's `onHome`/`app` (breadcrumb) props exist for this.
- fleet/DefectsPanel.tsx is one component rendered on four surfaces (trip detail, CreateTripWizard, the vehicle's Open Defects tab, and its ResolveDefectModal alone from InspectionDetailModal) — WARN-ONLY by design: it never reports "this vehicle has defects" to a parent, so no mount point can quietly become a block on trip creation or vehicle assignment. `onCreateWorkOrder` (an action, Open Defects tab only) and the `pendingWorkOrders`/`onPendingWorkOrdersSettled` marks that cover read-model lag are the only callbacks.
- ui/Chip.tsx StatusChip takes an optional `glyph` to separate two states that share one protected colour (a defect's Major and Out-of-Service are both vermillion) — an extra icon, never a new colour.
<!-- notes:dispatcher-components:end -->

<!-- notes:dispatcher-lib:start -->
- data.ts holds ALL mock data (the API seam — never invent endpoint shapes) · types.ts entity types · theme.ts color/typography tokens (extend it, no ad hoc colors) · nav.ts now holds only the ScreenId/NavItem/NavGroup types — NAV_GROUPS is derived from apps.ts, so a screen changes apps by editing the manifest, never nav.ts.
- apps.ts is the app manifest (APPS, canUseApp, appForScreen, railGroupsFor, appBadge): one `internal` app per NavRail group, plus the Budgeting tile as an `external` link whose href is the build-time NEXT_PUBLIC_BUDGETING_URL (unset renders "Not configured" rather than hiding the tile); it may only `import type` from nav.ts or the derivation becomes a cycle.
- roles.ts mirrors Backend/src/Shared/Kernel/Roles.cs (DISPATCH_ROLES, BUDGET_ROLES; legacy "Admin" normalises to Owner, matching is case-sensitive) — a UX gate for launcher tiles, not a boundary · appState.ts useRetainedState is a module-level Map so an app's list position survives the unmount that going Home causes; Console clears it on sign-out.
- billing/accruals.ts, reports/terminus.ts and booking/passes.ts are the pure derivations; the screen, the printed sheet (documents/accrualsPdf, terminusPdf, bookingPassPdf — NL-BP-01, one pass per page) and the email/clipboard payload all consume them rather than recompute. passes.ts also owns passIssuance gating and markPaidInput; passes are keyed by INDEX, not passenger id, because MARK AS PAID is a full-replacement PUT that re-creates passenger rows.
- claims.ts decodes the JWT payload WITHOUT signature verification — deliberate UX gate, not a security boundary (the API validates every request); claim names couple to Identity's JwtAccessTokenIssuer.cs, and Budgeting/lib/claims.ts is a twin that must stay in step.
- inspectionWorkOrder.ts owns the defect→work-order rules (attachable = open + on no OPEN work order; an unknown WO status counts as holding; prefills addressed by (inspectionId, item) — a defect has no id) · workOrderCompletion.ts mirrors the backend's WorkOrder.RecordOutcomes checks client-side and computes remainingBlockingDefects, which only ever gates a "Return to service" OFFER, never an automatic status change.
<!-- notes:dispatcher-lib:end -->
